learningObjective: Reason about the trade-off between compilation-time budget and end-to-end wall-clock savings across serving scenarios.
stem: A compiler exposes a knob 'tuning budget' (compilation time spent tuning) that trades off against runtime speed. Which statements about the trade-off are TRUE? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: For a one-off ad-hoc experiment (compile, run once, discard), tuning budget must be short; a slow compile that saves runtime only matters if runtime dominates.

Recompilation on shape changes (e.g., under `torch.compile` with recompiles enabled) can inflate the effective 'compile budget' well beyond the initial compile; the effective budget is per unique shape combination the runtime sees.
Tuning budget only affects the compiler and is orthogonal to serving latency; end-to-end latency is unaffected by tuning budget once the artifact is compiled.
For a model served millions of times per day, a longer tuning budget (hours) is easily amortized over serving lifetime; the wall-clock saving per request compounds.

explanation: Options A, B, D are correct; option C is incorrect. A (Correct): short-lived usage inverts the trade-off. B (Correct): recompilation is a hidden compile-budget line item. C (Wrong): tuning budget determines the artifact's runtime performance. D (Correct): amortization over serving lifetime. General context: C captures an important practical concern: recompilation costs are hidden 'compile budget' spent per unique shape/config the runtime encounters.

optionExplanations.A: Correct: short-lived usage inverts the trade-off.
optionExplanations.B: Correct: recompilation is a hidden compile-budget line item.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: tuning budget determines the artifact's runtime performance.

assumptions: The tuner and cost model behave as documented (convergent search).
nonImplications: Does not imply that longer budgets always improve runtime; measurement noise and cost-model plateaus can cap gains.
Does not imply short budgets are always sufficient — some workloads need substantial trials to leave a bad local optimum.

distractorRationales.C: Denies the causal path from tuning to runtime.
